paper.title: Blazar Variability as a Probe of Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Rays and Very-High-Energy Gamma Rays: A Multi-Messenger Review Across All Timescales
paper.abstract: Blazars are variable at every timescale that has been observed, from minute-scale flares to secular trends spanning decades, and across the whole electromagnetic spectrum from radio to very-high-energy (VHE; <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:semantics><mml:mrow><mml:msub><mml:mi>E</mml:mi><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi></mml:msub><mml:mo>≳</mml:mo><mml:mn>100</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:semantics></mml:math></inline-formula> GeV) <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:semantics><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi></mml:semantics></mml:math></inline-formula>-rays. This variability is not merely a nuisance to be averaged over: it is a time-resolved record of the physical conditions in the jet, and therefore a diagnostic of whether, and how, these sources accelerate particles to the highest energies. This review takes variability itself as its organizing principle. Rather than asking whether a particular blazar subclass accelerates ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), we ask what the amplitude, timescale, spectral evolution, inter-band correlation, and polarization behavior of blazar variability reveal about the underlying particle acceleration, and how that information bears on the production of VHE <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:semantics><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi></mml:semantics></mml:math></inline-formula>-rays and the acceleration of UHECRs. We organize the discussion by timescale, from microvariability through secular evolution, and by messenger, treating the electromagnetic light curves, the high-energy neutrino signal, and the (necessarily time-averaged) UHECR flux as complementary probes of the same accelerator. We review how causality arguments applied to rapid flares constrain the size, Doppler factor, and magnetic field of the emission region; how the presence or absence of inter-band correlation discriminates between leptonic and lepto-hadronic scenarios; and why the enormous magnetic time delays of charged cosmic rays sever the temporal link that neutrinos preserve. We close with the prospects that the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO), the Southern Wide-field Gamma-ray Observatory (SWGO), IceCube-Gen2, and the AugerPrime upgrade open for turning time-domain information into the identification of the astrophysical accelerators of the most energetic particles in the Universe.

paper.title: Quantifying Nighttime Gravity Wave-Driven Mesosphere-Ionosphere Coupling Over CONUS Using NASA AWE Radiance and GNSS TEC Observations
paper.abstract: We present the first coordinated study of nighttime mesosphere-ionosphere coupling over the continental United States (CONUS) from January through November 2024 using NASA Atmospheric Waves Experiment (AWE) airglow measurements near 87 km and GNSS Total Electron Content observations near 300 km. Coherent wave structures observed at both altitudes and high spatial correlations between their variances are used to identify strongly coupled events. Among 273 AWE swaths, ~65% exhibit strong coupling during quiet geomagnetic conditions, compared to ~23% during active times. The occurrence of strong coupling is negatively correlated with Kp and AE and positively correlated with Dst, indicating systematic modulation by geomagnetic activity. For strongly coupled events, GNSS-observed TIDs preferentially propagate northward, whereas only ~14% exhibit the classic southwestward propagation associated with Perkins instability. This northward preference is consistent with nighttime thermospheric wind filtering that favors poleward-propagating gravity waves. Our findings establish a quantitative baseline for nighttime mesosphere-ionosphere coupling.

paper.title: Weak Positive Discharges Leading to Lightning Initiation
paper.abstract: Lightning-initiating events in the Earth's atmosphere originate within compact regions of space with dimensions on the order of hundreds of meters. Growing observational evidence indicates that these discharges can also develop with much lower current magnitudes and substantially slower propagation speeds. Here we present a quantitative analysis of weak photoelectric feedback discharges (Pasko et al., 2025, https://doi.org/10.1029/2025JD043897) that provides an accurate quantitative interpretation of the available observations in terms of current moments, pulse durations, and positive breakdown velocities. Similarly to volt-ampere characteristics in conventional discharges the photoelectric feedback discharges exhibit a threshold type quadratic dependence on applied electric field explaining observed broad variability of parameters of these discharges.

paper.abstract: With the recent release of the largest gravitational-wave (GW) catalog to date --- the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-4.0) by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration --- a total of 218 candidate detections of GWs from compact binary coalescences (CBCs) have been reported. We use 142 of these 218 events with an false alarm rate smaller than 0.25 per year to investigate the impact of a novel parametric model to describe the full population mass spectrum of CBCs, on the estimation of the Hubble constant. This model is specially built to assess the importance of heavy black holes in GW cosmology. Our results are compared with the recent measurements reported by the LVK collaboration, both with spectral and dark sirens. With the spectral sirens, we estimate the Hubble constant to be H_0 = 81.6<SUP>+17.6</SUP> <SUB>-15.5</SUB> km s<SUP>-1</SUP> Mpc<SUP>-1</SUP> (at 68% C.L.), while the dark siren method yields H<SUB>0</SUB>=82.4<SUP>+16.9</SUP> <SUB>-13.3</SUB> km s<SUP>-1</SUP> Mpc<SUP>-1</SUP> (at 68% C.L.). These results represent improvements of approximately 32.9% and 38.1% in uncertainty, respectively. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this improvement is closely linked to the presence of an new additional mass scale for cosmology in the binary black hole (BBH) mass spectrum, found at 63.6<SUP>+4.5</SUP> <SUB>-4.9</SUB> M<SUB>⊙</SUB>. The inclusion of a new mass scale in the BH mass spectrum introduces additional constraints on the estimation of the Hubble constant, yielding precision comparable to that achieved by the two established mass scales at lower masses. Besides providing the tightest constraints on H<SUB>0</SUB> with standard sirens, it shows the importance of a new heavy mass feature in the BH spectrum.

paper.title: Observational signatures of rotating Ayón-Beato-García black holes: Shadows, accretion disks and images
paper.abstract: We investigate the shadows, accretion disks, and observational images of rotating Ayón-Beato-García (ABG) black holes with mass M, spin a, and nonlinear-electrodynamics (NLED) charge parameter ζ. The shadow shrinks with increasing ζ, which also modifies its deformation relative to the Kerr limit. Near-extremal configurations can exhibit a ``D''-shaped morphology, as Kerr black hole does. The thermal disk properties follow from the Novikov-Thorne model with inner edge at the innermost stable circular orbit, whereas the images use a separate, phenomenological optically thin emission model extending to the horizon. The image asymmetry and redshift maps depend strongly on (a, ζ) and the inclination. Comparing the geometric shadow diameters with the angular size intervals obtained from the EHT results for M87<SUP>*</SUP> and Sgr A<SUP>*</SUP> gives the indicative estimates ζ≲ 0.21 M and ζ≲ 0.43 M, respectively.

paper.title: Forecasting sensitivity to modified dispersion effects in pulsar timing arrays
paper.abstract: The pulsar timing array systems have reported a detection of a nanohertz-band stochastic gravitational wave background in our galaxy. It is of interest to use this observation to probe modified gravity and to forecast the sensitivity with which certain deviations can be tested in the coming years. In this paper, we focus on the modified dispersion relation of the tensor modes and its effect on the overlap reduction function of the timing residual cross-correlations. We perform a comprehensive forecast of the phase velocity uncertainty, σ<SUB>v</SUB> , using a Fisher analysis validated by a mock-data study to account for potential non-Gaussian behavior. We also take into account the sample variance effect and provide an observational timeline for future PTA sensitivity: detecting a 10% or -1% deviation from the speed of light at the 3σ level requires 𝒪(30) years of observations.

paper.title: Features of Ground Level Enhancement (GLE #74) Event on 11 May 2024
paper.abstract: Ground Level Enhancement (GLE #74) occurred on 11 May 2024 following an X5.8 solar flare from active region AR 13668 and the associated halo coronal mass ejection. The event was observed by both ground-based neutron monitors (NMs) and space-borne instruments and occurred during a deep Forbush decrease and one of the strongest geomagnetic storms of the current solar cycle, making its analysis particularly challenging. Using de-trended NM observations and explicitly accounting for storm-time variations in geomagnetic cutoff rigidity, we reconstructed the temporal evolution of the rigidity spectra and pitch-angle distributions of solar energetic particles (SEPs). The SEP rigidity spectra were moderately hard during the onset phase and exhibited a pronounced roll-off that gradually weakened as the event evolved, resulting in progressively softer spectra. The particle angular distribution revealed a significant anti-Sunward component and was best represented by a double-Gaussian pitch-angle distribution, suggesting complex interplanetary transport associated with disturbed magnetic field structures. The reconstructed SEP characteristics were in good overall agreement with GOES observations. These results provide new constraints on the acceleration and transport of high-energy SEPs during extreme space-weather events and demonstrate the robustness of NM-based SEP reconstructions under highly disturbed geomagnetic conditions.

paper.title: Investigation of Physical Mechanisms Driving EPB Poleward Regrowth and Equatorward Shrinkage/Erosion on the Substorm Night of 16 February 2013 Over China
paper.abstract: Equatorial plasma bubbles (EPBs) strongly impact space weather and radio propagation, yet their growth and erosion mechanisms, especially near midnight under weak geomagnetic activity, remain poorly understood. Using multi-source observations and model data, this work investigates an active EPB event extending poleward from 18°N over China on 16 February 2013 (Kp < 4, SYM/H > -20 nT). The results show that coupled substorm-time perturbation dynamo electric field (PDEF), likely arising from high-speed equatorward wind and relatively weaker residual substorm-driven prompt penetration electric field (PPEF), sustains EPB poleward regrowth within our region. Total eastward electric fields amplify the generalized Rayleigh-Taylor instability (GRTI) and facilitate EPB regrowth. Subsequent EPB erosion accompanies ionospheric decreases, plasma enhancement, and poleward-propagating brightness waves. These signatures arise from reversed poleward winds, which are likely produced by magnetically equatorial temperature enhancements driven by substorm-forced converging equatorward wind interactions. Quantitative analysis shows that atmospheric disturbance dynamo (ADD)-driven PDEF, enhanced by the residual substorm-PPEF, largely reproduces the EPB's poleward regrowth and clockwise rotation given locally reduced inclined Pedersen conductivity. Reversed poleward winds could compress dense plasma, forming fossilized bubbles. The active EPB originated from pre-existing bubbles likely produced by the sunset pre-reversal enhancement (PRE) mechanism, with their source region estimated to be 84°-86°E; alternatively, pre-existing bubbles may form west of our domain (near 90°E) at substorm onset, directly driven by substorm-PPEFs with a possible seed perturbation (e.g., atmospheric gravity waves) at the bottomside F-layer. This study highlights the dynamic processes governing EPB evolution through low-latitude wind-electric-field coupling under weak geomagnetic conditions over China.

paper.title: Thermospheric Responses to the Solar Flare on 5 May 2024 Over the 120°E Meridian Chain
paper.abstract: This study investigates thermospheric responses to the solar flare on 5 May 2024 by effectively disentangling their temporal evolution and spatial distribution using exospheric temperature (Tex) retrieved from multiple ionosonde stations and neutral density measurements from the GRACE-FO satellite. Following the flare onset, the ionosonde observations revealed pronounced and latitude-dependent responses with stronger electron density enhancements at Beijing, Wuhan and Mohe, but relatively weak response at Sanya. Together with total electron content observations, these results suggest that the background Equatorial Ionization Anomaly may have modulated the latitudinal distribution of the ionospheric response. The retrieved Tex also exhibited pronounced enhancements following the flare onset, with peak enhancements occurring approximately 45-60 min after the flare peak. This time lag was also observed in GRACE-FO neutral density. Notably, both the magnitude and timing of the thermospheric responses exhibited distinct latitudinal variations, with stronger warming at Beijing and earlier development at higher latitudes. These latitudinal differences indicate modulation by a common underlying physical driver, likely linked to the background Equatorial Mass Anomaly. A simplified heating model reproduced the delayed temporal evolution, indicating that the observed time lag is governed by cumulative flare-enhanced energy input rather than instantaneous flux, with radiative heating serving as the dominant driver for thermospheric responses. This work provides new insights into flare-induced thermospheric responses, advancing our understanding of solar-terrestrial interactions.

paper.title: Key Parameters for the Ionospheric Detection of Tsunamis From the 29 July 2025 Kamchatka Event
paper.abstract: It has been demonstrated that tsunamis generate internal gravity waves (GWs) detectable in the ionosphere within 20-60 min after their generation at the ocean surface. Despite numerous simulation and observation studies on ionospheric signatures of tsunamis, the detection of Co-tsunamic Ionospheric Disturbances (CTIDs) and distinguishing them from other Traveling Ionospheric Disturbances remain challenging. In this study, we used Total Electron Content (TEC) data from 69 GNSS receivers and 16 satellites (GLONASS, GALILEO, GPS) located at the Hawaii Islands to study the ionospheric response to the tsunami triggered by the 29 July 2025 Kamchatka earthquake. Our strategy for a reliable detection of CTID in TEC data series includes detrending, filtering and analysis of the power spectrum density. By using this technique, we identify two distinct signatures with a quasi-similar period of around 15-20 min, both occurring around the tsunami arrival time. However, analysis of spatio-temporal characteristics shows that the first disturbance propagates in a different direction with respect to the tsunami, and should be associated with the evening solar terminator that produces GWs and quasi-periodic ionospheric disturbances, similar to CTIDs. The second and stronger signal, is consistent with simulated tsunami propagation in terms of azimuth and timing. Its apparent propagation speed is about 280 m.${\mathrm{s}}^{-1}$, and the average amplitude is between -0.5 and 0.5 TECU. Therefore, estimating the direction of propagation, speed, period, and frequency is necessary to confirm a CTID.

paper.title: Ionospheric Disturbances Associated With Typhoon Ragasa in 2025 Observed Using GNSS and Satellite Measurements
paper.abstract: Typhoon Ragasa in September 2025 provides an opportunity to examine ionospheric responses to tropical cyclone forcing from the lower atmosphere. We combine Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations over Taiwan and Hong Kong with Himawari-9 thermal infrared (TIR) data, COSMIC-2 radio occultation profiles, TIMED/GUVI thermospheric composition measurements, and Horizontal Wind Model 2014 (HWM14) winds. Under stable solar and quiet to weakly disturbed geomagnetic conditions, persistent medium-scale traveling ionospheric disturbances were detected, with phase speeds of 160-271 m/s and detrended total electron content (dTEC) amplitudes of ±0.4-0.5 TECU. TIR ripples were aligned with dTEC wavefronts 560-1,120 km from the typhoon center, supporting a connection between deep convection and the observed ionospheric disturbances. Regional mean dTEC variability during the typhoon was comparable to later variability, and the rate of TEC (ROT) excursions was similar before, during, and after the event, whereas the rate of TEC index (ROTI) transiently increased to about 1.4 TECU/min. Enhanced ROTI along PRN 08 and PRN 27 occurred when ionospheric pierce points sampled the 600-800 km region containing organized TIR perturbations. COSMIC-2 profiles showed electron density enhancement at 15°-30°N and depletion at 0°-15°N, indicating a latitude dependent plasma response. HWM14 showed weaker and smoother winds in the mesosphere and larger vertical variability above 90 km, providing background context for the propagation and dissipation of gravity waves. TIMED/GUVI showed no pronounced large scale O/N2 depletion. Together, these observations support Ragasa associated wave forcing as an important contributor to multiscale ionospheric response.

paper.title: Models of exponential and power-law acceleration of the Universe in Horndeski theory without ghosts and Laplace instabilities
paper.abstract: We present a designer method for flat Friedman-Robertson-Walker spacetimes within the framework of Horndeski’s scalar-tensor theory. In this method, as ansatzes, we use the following assumptions. First, we set the propagation speeds cT, cS in the tensor and scalar sectors of perturbations, the tensor-to-scalar ratio r and other perturbation parameters to be constant. Following the observational data, we believe that 1−3⋅10−15<cT<1, 0<r<0.1 (LIGO Scientific Collab., Virgo Collab. and Fermi Gamma-Ray Burst Monitor Team, Astrophys. J. Lett. 848, L13 (2017)). This ansatz allows us to exclude ghosts and Laplace instabilities at the initial stage. Second, we choose the dependence of the Hubble parameter on the derivative of the scalar field H(ϕ̇). Since the characteristics of perturbations cT, cS and others are initially expressed through H, ϕ̇ and the Horndeski potentials, the ansatzes with the gravity equations give a system of differential equations for the scalar field and the unknown Horndeski potentials. Knowledge of H(ϕ̇) and ϕ̇(t) gives the law of the Universe expansion a(t). As a result, one can find subclasses of Horndeski’s scalar-tensor theory within which cosmological solutions exist without ghosts and Laplace instabilities. As an example, we found subclasses of Horndeski’s theory for exponential and power-law inflation models of the Universe without pathologies.

paper.title: Fractional corrections to black hole spacetimes: Invariant formulation, quasinormal modes, and evaporation in Schwarzschild, Reissner-Nordström, and Kerr geometries
paper.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the consequences of a fully invariant formulation of fractional gravity on classical black hole spacetimes. Starting from a fractional action in which the fractional parameter is promoted to a dynamical scalar field, we derive the exact Schwarzschild solution as the ground state of the theory, ensuring diffeomorphism invariance and the conservation of the energy-momentum tensor. Allowing the fractional parameter to vary spatially introduces controlled corrections to the metric, effectively modifying the black hole mass function and horizon structure. We compute analytic WKB approximations for quasinormal modes, highlighting shifts in both real and imaginary frequencies due to fractional corrections. Hawking temperature and entropy are correspondingly modified, yielding corrections to the black hole evaporation rate. We extend these results to charged Reissner-Nordström and rotating Kerr black holes, deriving analytic estimates for quasinormal modes, horizon shifts, and temperature corrections within the fractional framework. Our results demonstrate that fractional modifications provide a consistent, covariant generalization of classical black hole physics, offering a novel avenue for exploring semiclassical and phenomenological implications of fractional geometry.

paper.title: Quasinormal modes of Kerr-like black bounce spacetime
paper.abstract: We investigate the quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum of a Kerr-like black-bounce spacetime under massive scalar-field perturbations. Starting from the Kerr-like deformation of the Simpson-Visser black-bounce geometry, we derive the corresponding radial and angular equations and obtain the effective potential governing scalar perturbations. The QNM frequencies are computed by means of the Pöschl-Teller potential approximation and the semi-analytic WKB method (up to sixth order), and we demonstrate reasonable agreement between these two approaches. We then analyze in detail how the QNM spectrum depends on the spin parameter a, the bounce parameter p that interpolates between black hole and wormhole geometries, and the scalar-field mass μ. Our results show that increasing the spin parameter a raises the oscillation frequency, while increasing the bounce parameter p lowers it, and in both cases the damping rate decreases. Moreover, the mass of the scalar field has a non-negligible impact on the ringdown spectrum. These features suggest that rotating black-bounce geometries may leave distinct imprints in the ringdown phase of gravitational-wave signals, and motivate future studies of echoes and parameter estimation in the context of present and upcoming detectors.

paper.title: A self-shadowing black hole accretion disk at sub-Eddington luminosities
paper.abstract: Accretion onto black holes powers some of the most energetic sources in the Universe, yet its behaviour across the luminosity range remains poorly understood. Specifically, as the luminosity approaches the Eddington limit (L<SUB>Edd</SUB>), the inner accretion disk is expected to depart from the standard thin-disk solution, becoming vertically extended. The luminosity threshold and observational signatures of this transition remain, however, uncertain. We present multiwavelength spectroscopy obtained during the decay of a black hole X-ray binary outburst. At the peak (~0.2 L<SUB>Edd</SUB>), a cool optical and near-infrared spectrum dominated by strong recombination lines of hydrogen and He I is observed. However, as the luminosity decreases, it switches to a hot, highly irradiated, nearly featureless spectrum. This puzzling behaviour reveals the emergence of a vertically extended inner disk at the outburst peak, shielding the outer regions from high-energy radiation produced near the black hole—a scenario supported by contemporaneous X-ray spectra. Observations of similar systems suggest that this phenomenon may be common among black hole accretion disks. Self-shadowing structures at luminosities well below L<SUB>Edd</SUB> have major implications for black hole accretion flows and their observational properties, affecting inferred black hole spins, X-ray polarization measurements and the physical conditions of the outer disk and its associated outflows.

paper.title: An intertwined short and long γ-ray burst with a 4-minute separation
paper.abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), among the most energetic transients in the Universe, are traditionally classified into long-duration (lasting more than 2 seconds) and short-duration (lasting less than 2 seconds) events. Long-duration GRBs are typically associated with the core collapse of massive stars (type II), whereas short-duration GRBs originate from the merger of compact binary systems (type I). These different progenitor channels are reflected in distinct observational signatures that provide key diagnostics for GRB classification. Here we report a peculiar event, GRB 160425A, comprising two sub-bursts separated by 4 minutes: a short-duration burst (G<SUB>1</SUB>) and a long-duration burst (G<SUB>2</SUB>). Nearly all standard prompt-emission diagnostics, including pulse morphology, duration, hardness ratio, minimum variability timescale, spectral properties and established empirical correlations, consistently categorize G<SUB>1</SUB> as a short-like GRB (type I, merger origin) and G<SUB>2</SUB> as a long-like (type II, collapsar origin) GRB. The coexistence of merger and collapsar signatures within a single event challenges existing progenitor frameworks and calls for a re-evaluation of GRB classification schemes and progenitor scenarios.

paper.title: AMPy: A Flexible Framework for Modeling Gamma-Ray Burst Afterglows
paper.abstract: The most powerful and energetic explosions in the known universe---gamma-ray bursts (GRBs)---originate from the collapse of massive stars or the merger of compact objects. Often marking the birth of a black hole, GRBs produce broadband emission via synchrotron radiation as the resulting ultra-relativistic jet interacts with the surrounding medium. This emission, known as the afterglow, carries rich information about the nature of the burst and its environment. Yet, despite strong theoretical motivation, and mounting observational evidence, for diverse density structures, many existing modeling tools remain tied to fixed environmental prescriptions (e.g., constant-density or idealized stellar-wind profiles) and lack flexible, unified approaches for statistical inference and model comparison. To address these limitations, we present AMPy (Afterglow Modeling in Python), a modular framework for Bayesian inference that combines a highly optimized, analytic forward-shock model that supports arbitrary power-law density profiles with a statistical framework that consistently incorporates systematic and statistical uncertainties across heterogeneous and multi-wavelength datasets. AMPy also supports seamless integration of user-defined models through a plugin architecture, allowing competing physical prescriptions to be evaluated and compared within an identical inference pipeline. We demonstrate the modeling capabilities on the multi-wavelength dataset of GRB 221009A and show that AMPy serves as an end-to-end toolkit for parameter estimation, model testing, and interpreting the environments and physics of GRBs.

paper.title: The Potential of the THESEUS Mission for Studies of Young Stellar Objects
paper.abstract: THESEUS is a proposed ESA M-class mission primarily designed for high-redshift gamma-ray burst studies, but its wide-field survey strategy and multi-instrument payload also offer significant opportunities for time-domain investigations of Galactic young stellar objects (YSOs). We assess the mission's potential for YSO science by examining the detectability of energetic X-ray flares, the observability of Galactic star-forming regions, and the benefits of coordinated soft X-ray and near-infrared observations. Instrument characteristics are combined with literature-based YSO population estimates and Orion-derived flare statistics. SXI exposure maps are used to estimate region-dependent cumulative temporal coverage, while IRT crowding is characterized through nearest-neighbor separations relative to the expected EE50 and EE80 angular scales. The detailed distribution of the cumulative SXI exposure among individual observing intervals is not yet specified and is therefore treated separately as a temporal-sampling uncertainty, while additional sensitivity tests quantify the effects of flare duration and X-ray absorption. Using Orion as a benchmark, we derive comparative, model-dependent estimates indicating that THESEUS may detect substantial samples of energetic YSO flares during its nominal mission lifetime. A substantial fraction of sources are expected to have nearest-neighbor separations larger than the adopted IRT EE-based angular scales even in crowded regions, although unique source identification from SXI data alone may be challenging. THESEUS can therefore serve both as a transient discovery instrument and as a statistical probe of YSO high-energy variability.

paper.title: Initial performance of the Radar Echo Telescope for Cosmic Rays: Pathfinder for a next-generation neutrino detector
paper.abstract: The Radar Echo Telescope for Cosmic Rays, a pathfinder instrument for the radar echo method of ultrahigh energy neutrino detection, was initially deployed near Summit Station, Greenland, in May 2023. After a four-week commissioning period, nine days of data were taken before the instrument went offline. In this article, we describe the instrument as it was deployed, and the initial performance of the detector. We show that the technical aspects of running a radar-based particle cascade detector in the ice have been demonstrated. Analysis of the 2023 data informed improvements that were incorporated into the May--August 2024 deployment, which has just concluded at time of writing. Results from the 2024 run will be presented in forthcoming publications.

paper.title: Deep learning search for gravitational waves from compact binary coalescence
paper.abstract: Gravitational-wave searches rely on a combination of methods, including matched filtering, coherent analyses, and more recent machine-learning--based pipelines. For compact binary coalescences---where signals originate from the relativistic dynamics of compact objects---matched filtering remains a central element, but its computational cost will increase substantially with the data volumes and parameter-space coverage required by next-generation interferometers such as the Einstein Telescope. Developing complementary strategies that reduce computational load while preserving detection performance is therefore essential. We investigate a hybrid approach that combines matched-filtering concepts with convolutional neural networks, enabling efficient signal searches without relying on the usual <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:msup><mml:mi>χ</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:msup></mml:math></inline-formula> rejection test. Using simulated datasets that include injected signals in Gaussian noise, transient noise, and physical effects not represented in the template bank---such as eccentricity, precession and higher-order modes---we show that the method achieves a detection efficiency comparable to or better than a standard matched-filtering search while offering a more resource-efficient pipeline in all the cases where the physics included in the signals were not represented in the template bank or when glitches were affecting the data. Conversely, the analysis also reveals some loss of detection capability for standard binary neutron star and binary black hole searches in pure Gaussian noise. These results indicate that deep-learning--assisted searches can support sustainable gravitational-wave data analysis in future detector eras.

paper.title: Population-level correlations in Bayesian statistics: An illustrative model for gravitational-wave astronomy
paper.abstract: With increasingly large numbers of gravitational-wave events, population inference is now beginning to move beyond predictions of marginal distributions and to probe correlations between compact-binary parameters such as masses, spins, and redshifts. These correlations have strong constraining power for both astrophysics and tests of general relativity. In this paper, we present an idealized analytical model to study the interplay between single-event correlations, systematic biases, and population-level correlations. With this, we investigate the potential emergence of false-positive measurements of population-level correlations. We quantify how the presence of correlations at the single-event level between a pair of parameters increases the uncertainty of population-level correlations for those parameters, potentially obscuring the true underlying population correlation if present. We also find that if waveform systematics lead to biases that are correlated across the catalog (which is likely, because certain regions of the parameter space are more difficult to model), this can be effectively absorbed by a population analysis that targets correlations and can be misinterpreted as such. This simple Gaussian-based model may serve as a broad compass for future, more detailed explorations.

paper.title: Autoencoder-based surrogate waveform model for quasicircular binary-black-hole mergers
paper.abstract: The generation of accurate waveforms from binary black hole (BBH) mergers is a major effort in gravitational-wave astronomy. In recent years, machine-learning-based surrogate models for BBH waveforms have been proposed. Those offer the potential to dramatically accelerate waveform generation while maintaining accuracy competitive with that of traditional waveform approximants. In this work, we investigate the viability of autoencoders as generative models for gravitational-wave signals from quasicircular BBH mergers. We introduce AESur3dq8, a novel surrogate waveform model based on autoencoders that enables the rapid and accurate construction of large template banks, producing millions of waveforms in under a second using modest computational resources. The model is trained on the numerical-relativity-informed surrogate NRHybSur3dq8 and subsequently fine-tuned using the simulating extreme spacetimes catalog of BBH simulations. We demonstrate that waveforms generated by AESur3dq8 achieve mismatches of order <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:msup><mml:mn>10</mml:mn><mml:mrow><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mn>4</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup></mml:math></inline-formula> with respect to numerical relativity waveforms, and that parameter estimation performed with these templates yields results fully consistent with those reported by the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory, Virgo, and Kamioka Gravitational Wave Detector Collaboration for observed gravitational-wave events.

paper.title: Probing primordial black hole mergers in clusters with pulsar timing data
paper.abstract: We consider the possibility that the stochastic gravitational wave (GW) background suggested by pulsar timing array (PTA) datasets is sourced by primordial black holes (PBHs). Specifically, we perform a Bayesian search in the International PTA data release 2 (IPTA DR2) for a combined GW background arising from scalar perturbations and unresolved PBH mergers, assuming a broad PBH mass distribution. In our analysis, we incorporate constraints on the curvature power spectrum from cosmic microwave background <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mi>μ</mml:mi></mml:math></inline-formula> distortions and the overproduction of PBHs, which significantly suppress the contribution of PBH mergers to the total GW background. We find that scalar-induced GWs dominate the nanohertz frequency range, while PBH mergers alone cannot account for the observed signal under the standard PBH formation scenario involving Gaussian perturbations and including only Poissonian PBH clustering. However, specific PBH models, such as those with enhanced clustering, could yield a GW background dominated by PBH mergers. Overall, we find that the IPTA DR2 strongly favors an astrophysical origin for the reported common-spectrum process over the PBH models considered in this analysis.

paper.title: CMB bounds on primordial black holes via radiation capture

paper.title: Perturbations in the parametrized wormhole spacetime and their related quasinormal modes
paper.abstract: We study electromagnetic perturbations and the associated quasinormal modes (QNMs) of parametrized static, spherically symmetric wormhole spacetimes, focusing on Damour-Solodukhin and braneworld geometries as well as their galactic extensions. Using the Bronnikov-Konoplya-Pappas (BKP) parametrization, we express the metric functions in terms of a compactified radial coordinate and characterize the spacetime through far-field and near-throat parameters. The far-field coefficients govern the asymptotic structure and post-Newtonian behavior, while the near-throat continued-fraction expansion captures the strong-field geometry near the throat. We first apply the parametrization to isolated wormholes and identify its range of validity, showing that the nonanalytic metric functions can limit the applicability of the BKP scheme. Moreover we have shown that such issues can indeed hamper the primary ringdown waveform. We then extend the framework to a galactic Damour-Solodukhin wormhole embedded in a Hernquist dark matter halo. Imposing observational bounds from the shadow of Sgr <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi>A</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mo>*</mml:mo></mml:msup></mml:math></inline-formula>, we constrain the galactic compactness and deformation parameters and obtain an observationally viable parametrized metric. Within the allowed parameter space, we compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using the transfer matrix method and analyze the corresponding time-domain ringdown signals. We find that the damping rate is more sensitive to galactic compactness, whereas the oscillation frequency remains comparatively stable. Although the spectral shifts are small within the shadow-allowed region, the framework provides a systematic link between geometric parametrization, shadow constraints, and dynamical response. Our results establish an observationally consistent parametrized description of wormhole perturbations for strong-field tests of horizonless compact objects.

paper.title: Efficient eccentric effective-one-body dynamics via near-identity averaging transformations
paper.abstract: Next-generation gravitational-wave detectors, such as LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and Cosmic Explorer, will require accurate and efficient models of long-lived black hole binary signals, including those with significant eccentricity. A challenge for eccentric effective-one-body (EOB) models is the cost of resolving rapidly oscillating orbital dynamics over the inspiral, particularly for low-mass and large-mass-ratio systems. We address this by recasting the nonspinning eccentric effective-one-body equations of motion in terms of osculating orbital elements and then applying near-identity averaging transformations to eliminate the fast orbital-timescale structure during the inspiral. Each order in this procedure suppresses the oscillatory behavior by one factor of the ratio of orbital to radiation-reaction timescales. The resulting averaged dynamics are evolved on the radiation-reaction timescale, and then, the system is mapped back to the full EOB dynamics for the final transition to plunge. This reduces the cost of the inspiral dynamics by up to 2 orders of magnitude, eliminating this as the primary bottleneck for long waveforms. The overall waveform-generation speedup spans <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1.5</mml:mn><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mn>8</mml:mn><mml:mo>×</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:math></inline-formula>, motivating the development of more efficient waveform-generation methods. We also validate the accuracy of the method by comparing waveforms generated from the averaged and full effective-one-body dynamics across a broad region of parameter space for moderate to large eccentricities. Carrying out this averaging procedure to next-to-next-to-leading order is needed to accurately model comparable-mass binaries, yielding mismatches <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mo><=</mml:mo><mml:mn>8.05</mml:mn><mml:mo>×</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mn>10</mml:mn><mml:mrow><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mn>5</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup></mml:math></inline-formula>. paper.title: Merger remnant and eccentricity dynamics surrogates for eccentric nonspinning black hole binaries
paper.abstract: Accurate models of merger remnants are increasingly important for gravitational-wave science, including precision tests of gravity with ringdown, inference of black-hole populations, and modeling hierarchical mergers. For eccentric binaries, remnant mass, spin, and recoil carry nontrivial imprints of eccentricity that are both physically informative and more challenging to model, yet remain less developed than in the quasicircular case. We present two new models trained on numerical-relativity (NR) simulations of unequal-mass, nonspinning eccentric binary black holes: NRSurE_q4NoSpin_Remnant, which predicts remnant properties, and NRSurE_q4NoSpin_Dynamics, a time-domain surrogate for the evolution of eccentricity and mean anomaly. Both models are trained on NR simulations over a three-dimensional parameter space with mass ratios <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mi>q</mml:mi><mml:mo><=</mml:mo><mml:mn>4</mml:mn></mml:math></inline-formula>, eccentricity <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mi>e</mml:mi><mml:mo><</mml:mo><mml:mn>0.23</mml:mn></mml:math></inline-formula>, and mean anomaly <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mo>ℓ</mml:mo><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:mo>[</mml:mo><mml:mn>0</mml:mn><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mn>2</mml:mn><mml:mi>π</mml:mi><mml:mo>)</mml:mo></mml:math></inline-formula> radians, where both <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mi>e</mml:mi></mml:math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mo>ℓ</mml:mo></mml:math></inline-formula> are defined at <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mi>t</mml:mi><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mn>1000</mml:mn><mml:mi>M</mml:mi></mml:math></inline-formula> relative to peak amplitude and <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mi>M</mml:mi></mml:math></inline-formula> is the total mass. We highlight some applications, including the phenomenological impact of eccentricity on remnant properties and the enhancement or suppression of recoil. We also provide error estimates for all modeled quantities, supporting reliable use in current and future gravitational-wave parameter-estimation analyses. Both models will be made available through open-source codes.

paper.title: Searching for a waveform-agnostic gravitational wave signal in pulsar timing arrays
paper.abstract: Pulsar timing arrays have recently provided strong evidence for a nanohertz stochastic gravitational wave background, motivating searches for deterministic gravitational wave signals from localized sources. Most existing searches assume specific waveform templates, which can be potentially insensitive to unexpected signals. We introduce a waveform-agnostic framework that models signal-induced timing residuals via a Fourier expansion. A Lorentzian profile is imposed on the variances of the Fourier coefficients, providing a flexible spectral envelope that captures the signal's dominant frequency and bandwidth while remaining agnostic to its exact shape. Analytical marginalization over the Fourier coefficients then yields a Bayesian hierarchical framework that concurrently infers the source sky location, its frequency content, and the stochastic background. To mitigate contamination from unmodeled pulsar noise, we also include a pulsar-specific excess process with a frequency-independent power spectrum for the timing residuals. Tests on simulated datasets show that the method is robust and provides a flexible tool for future pulsar timing array searches, with sensitivity to both expected and unexpected gravitational wave phenomena.

paper.title: Polarization analysis of ringdown signals
paper.abstract: Merging binary black holes exhibit a ringdown phase in which they primarily emit gravitational waves in the shape of damped sinusoids corresponding to quasinormal modes of the Kerr remnant. In general, each mode carries 4 degrees of freedom encoding amplitude and phase information. When the modes are excited with equatorial reflection symmetry, as is the case for black hole mergers with spins (anti)aligned to the orbital angular momentum, the symmetry constrains 2 degrees of freedom. As a result, the relationship between polarization amplitudes and phases in each mode is fixed by the viewing (inclination) angle to the equatorial plane. We use such a constrained model to fit the ringdown signals of both nonprecessing and precessing systems such as GW150914 and GW190521, respectively. We show that we can measure the degree of circular polarization and handedness of ringdown signals like those of GW150914, even if only the two LIGO detectors are available; such a polarization measurement can be translated into an inferred source inclination assuming the reflection symmetry above, again using the ringdown signal alone. On the other hand, the constrained polarization model is insufficient to capture the polarization structure of signals from precessing systems, leading to biases in the inferred mode frequencies and amplitudes. We explore the magnitude of this effect by fitting GW190521-like injections with the restricted model, finding weaker predictive accuracy relative to the arbitrary-polarization model and potentially significant systematic biases. As our detectors continue to improve, using the correct polarization model is increasingly important to avoid biased ringdown measurements.

paper.title: Black hole-neutron star binaries with high spins and large mass asymmetries. III. Properties of the ejected material and its electromagnetic signatures
paper.abstract: Compact binary systems consisting of a black hole (BH) and a neutron star (NS) are expected to provide detectable signals both in the gravitational-wave and in the electromagnetic channels, thus representing excellent sources for multimessenger astronomy. In this third paper in a series, we report on the geometric and thermodynamic properties of the purely dynamical ejecta component modeled in our general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamical simulations of BHNS systems over a comprehensive binary parameter space consisting of large mass ratio and high BH spin. The tidal disruption and dynamical mass ejection is studied by monitoring the transfer of energy and angular momentum to matter for the particular case of a highly unequal-mass binary with large BH spin, extending known results for low-mass-ratio, irrotational BHNS binaries. By varying the binary parameters, we investigate their influence on the geometric, thermodynamic, and kinematic properties of the ejected matter. Furthermore, we employ the nuclear-reaction network SkyNet to obtain the elemental abundances resulting from the <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mi>r</mml:mi></mml:math></inline-formula> process active in the ejecta and study how they depend on the properties of the progenitor objects. Finally, using the radiative-transfer code POSSIS, we compute the kilonova light curves from the results of our simulations, discuss their bolometric and optical/near-infrared evolution, and compare them with the AT2017gfo data and upper limits for S190814bv, finding overall consistency.

paper.title: Massive scalar fields in eccentric regime: Detectability and constraints from LISA observations of extreme mass-ratio inspirals
paper.abstract: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are among the most promising sources for future space-based gravitational wave (GW) observatories and provide sensitive probes of additional fundamental fields in the strong-gravity regime. In the present work, we investigate eccentric equatorial EMRIs around Kerr black holes in the presence of a massive scalar field. We assume that the inspiraling object carries a scalar charge and, therefore, emits scalar radiation in addition to GWs. By solving the massive scalar perturbation equation in the frequency domain, we compute the relativistic scalar energy fluxes at the event horizon and at infinity and incorporate them into an adiabatic inspiral model. We investigate the impact of the scalar charge and scalar-field mass on the orbital evolution and gravitational waveforms by analyzing the accumulated phase differences and waveform mismatches relative to both general relativity and the massless scalar limit. Our results show that the massive scalar radiation can produce significant GW dephasing, with the effect becoming increasingly pronounced for more eccentric orbits. In addition, the scalar flux is suppressed for larger scalar-field masses as fewer scalar harmonics satisfy the propagation condition at infinity. Finally, using both Fisher information matrix forecasts and Bayesian parameter estimation, we assess the capability of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna to constrain the scalar charge and scalar-field mass. The two inference approaches gives consistent constraints, demonstrating that eccentric EMRIs provide a promising avenue for probing massive scalar fields and scalar-tensor extensions of gravity in the strong-field regime.

paper.title: Quasilinear Theory of Fast Flavor Instabilities
paper.abstract: Dense neutrino plasmas can develop instabilities that drive collisionless flavor exchange, equivalent to the emission of flavomons, the quanta of flavor waves. We treat these waves as independent linear degrees of freedom and develop a quasilinear theory, including backreaction on the neutrino distribution and nonresonant neutrino-flavomon interactions, while neglecting wave-wave processes. In a statistically homogeneous, axisymmetric model, the saturated neutrino and flavomon distributions agree closely with periodic-box solutions of the original quantum kinetic equation. Our results provide the first theoretical interpretation for the numerical observations. They also show that flavomon phases have little influence on the final state, supporting the quasilinear theory as a framework for capturing flavor evolution without resolving nonlinear small-scale dynamics.

paper.title: Accreting Stellar-Mass Black Holes
paper.abstract: Accreting stellar-mass black holes exhibit dramatic variability across the electromagnetic spectrum, including spectral state transitions, outbursts, and jet production, making them unique laboratories for understanding accretion processes in strong gravitational fields. This review synthesizes recent progress in understanding these systems, focusing on their continuum emission, timing properties, emission lines, and X-ray polarization. A complex interplay between the accretion disk, the so-called corona, and jet underlies the observed spectral and timing behavior, with quasi-periodic oscillations and broadband noise providing windows into the dynamics of the innermost accretion flow. Emission lines across all wavelengths serve as critical diagnostics of the disk structure, outflows, and reprocessing, while iron K lines in the X-ray band probe the properties of the inner disk through relativistic reflection. Polarization studies suggest that the corona is likely extended perpendicular to the jet axis in the hard state, while the soft state remains poorly understood, with observations that do not yet conform to simple theoretical expectations; a puzzle that continues to challenge our interpretation of accretion geometry. Despite significant advances, fundamental questions remain about the physical origins of state transitions, the role of magnetic fields in driving outflows and shaping the accretion flow, and the connection between disk instabilities and jet launching. This review underscores the need for future multi-wavelength, timing, and polarimetric studies to deepen our understanding of accretion physics in strong-gravity environments.

paper.title: Solar Flare Forecasting Using the Spatial Distributions of Active Region Properties
paper.abstract: Solar flares (SF) are energetic solar events that can influence space weather and disrupt space-based technologies. Many data-driven forecasting models rely on parameterized, hand-engineered features derived from active regions (ARs). However, such parameterization compresses the spatial structure of ARs and may discard information relevant to flare initiation. In this work, we investigate the spatial distributions of several AR properties for flare forecasting using deep convolutional neural networks. To standardize input dimensions across ARs, we propose a resizing technique called Pad-crop. Our results show that models trained on different physical properties achieve comparable forecasting performance, indicating that the morphology of ARs in-its-own may encode meaningful flare signatures. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis further indicates that the models focus on physically meaningful zones of the ARs, suggesting that relevant features are being captured. In addition, an analysis of false-positive predictions suggests that intermediate C-class flares during the prediction window may contribute to model confusion. These findings highlight the importance of the spatial structure in AR properties and motivate further exploration of morphology-based approaches for SF forecasting. The source code associated with this work will be made publicly available.

paper.title: A Finite Universe as a Laboratory for Quantum Gravity
paper.abstract: We explore a model in which the observed FLRW cosmology admits a finite global completion and ask how this affects prospects for testing quantum gravity. A finite overdense region embedded in a larger background can collapse gravitationally, providing a prehistory for the observed expansion. If the collapse approaches a finite quantum-supported density <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:semantics><mml:msub><mml:mi>ρ</mml:mi><mml:mi>G</mml:mi></mml:msub></mml:semantics></mml:math></inline-formula>, positive spatial curvature permits a nonsingular bounce connecting contraction to expansion. Such a cosmology can act as a laboratory for quantum gravity. We use quadratic gravity and PT-symmetric quantum theory as concrete realizations while emphasizing that the strategy is more general. The CMB amplitude of fluctuations constrains the cuadratic coupling, while large-angle CMB parity statistics and particle--antiparticle asymmetry can be related to an effective PT-breaking amplitude. PT completion also suggests a connection to the arrow of time: information inaccessible within one semiclassical branch may remain encoded in a unitary PT-complete quantum state, potentially reformulating aspects of the Past Hypothesis and apparent information loss. The contracting phase provides a second source of structure. Nonlinear structures formed before the bounce may survive behind the particle horizon, with their abundance and mass function constrained by dark matter, early supermassive black holes, lensing and gravitational waves. Strong-gravity measurements provide complementary tests through black-hole perturbations, horizon absorption and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals. The framework is therefore a network of cross-consistency and falsification tests. Cosmological maps, black holes and gravitational waves can be viewed as experiments in regimes inaccessible to terrestrial laboratories, providing an observational approach to quantum gravity complementary to microscopic theory building.
categories: quantum field theory in curved spacetime

paper.title: Multiwavelength Timing Analysis of the Recurrent Nova T CrB
paper.abstract: We present a short-timescale multiwavelength timing study of the symbiotic recurrent nova T Coronae Borealis (T CrB), based on Swift/X-Ray Telescope (XRT), Swift/UltraViolet Optical Telescope (UVOT), and Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) observations obtained across the high state, the 2023--2024 optical/UV dip, and the subsequent recovery. We use high-cadence event-mode and TESS data to search specifically for sub-kilosecond variability and simultaneous UV--optical correlations. The UVM2 event-mode data show a candidate variability timescale near 445 s during MJD 59,954.1--60,276.9. The folded extrema correspond to a descriptive fractional modulation amplitude of about 9.9%. The feature remains at approximately the same timescale when 20 s, 10 s, and 5 s event-mode bins are used, while no corresponding 445 s peak is found in the spacecraft-pointing diagnostic, the background light curve, or a nearby comparison star. Nevertheless, we do not establish phase coherence across observations separated by days to weeks, and no UVW1 or UVW2 event-mode data are available for an equivalent high-cadence test; the feature is therefore treated as a tentative QPO-like timescale rather than a secure coherent period. No significant 445 s peak is present in the XRT or TESS Lomb--Scargle periodograms. Injection--recovery tests give a 90% coherent-sinusoid fractional semi-amplitude sensitivity of about 34.3% for the 0.3--10 keV XRT light curve and cadence-corrected limits of about 0.054%, 0.056%, 0.022%, and 0.012% for TESS Sectors 24, 25, 51, and 78, respectively. The only strictly contemporaneous UVM2--TESS Sector 78 overlap spans JD 2,460,442.1159722--2,460,442.1260764 (873 s); after excluding the final incomplete UVM2 bin, 840 s is used for the cross-correlation function (CCF). A phenomenological Gaussian fit to the CCF trough gives a dimensionless coefficient of <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:semantics><mml:mrow><mml:mo>-</mml:mo><mml:mn>0.41</mml:mn><mml:mo>±</mml:mo><mml:mn>0.09</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:semantics></mml:math></inline-formula> and a lag of <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:semantics><mml:mrow><mml:mn>84</mml:mn><mml:mo>±</mml:mo><mml:mn>31</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:semantics></mml:math></inline-formula> s (90% confidence; <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:semantics><mml:mrow><mml:mo>∆</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mi>χ</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:msup><mml:mo>=</mml:mo><mml:mn>2.7</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:semantics></mml:math></inline-formula>). The sign of the anti-correlation persists after simple linear and quadratic detrending, although the inferred lag is sensitive to detrending and edge effects. We therefore regard both the 445 s feature and the UV--optical lag as tentative. The present data do not uniquely identify the emitting regions or establish a propagation mechanism. These results highlight T CrB as a valuable target for simultaneous high-cadence ultraviolet, optical, and X-ray monitoring before and during its next nova eruption.

paper.title: GW170817 viable Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Higgs inflation confronted with ACT
paper.abstract: In this work, we shall consider Higgs inflationary Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theories that are compatible with the GW170817 event, which dictates that the gravitational wave speed of primordial tensor perturbations must satisfy the constraint |cT2 − 1| < 6 × 10−15. We consider Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theories that yield directly cT2 = 1 for which theories, the scalar potential and the non-minimal Gauss-Bonnet scalar coupling function are related. We assume that the non-minimal Gauss-Bonnet scalar coupling function is identical with the Higgs potential, and we confront the resulting theory with the ACT data, to determine whether the theory is viable. As we show, the resulting theoretical framework is viable and compatible with the ACT data and the updated Planck constraints on the tensor-to-scalar ratio.

paper.title: On the Role of Gravity in Supercooled Phase Transitions
paper.abstract: Theories with radiative mass generation and radiative symmetry breaking (RSB) lead to first-order phase transitions (FOPTs) and the production of gravitational waves (GWs) as well as primordial black holes if supercooling lasts long enough. Here we investigate the role of gravity in supercooled FOPTs that occur in the RSB scenario. We use a model-independent approach that is valid when a quantity (which we explicitly determine and is computable once the model is specified) is small enough. Eventually, the curvature of spacetime becomes relevant if the FOPT does not complete in the case in which gravity is ignored. We also include the effect on the FOPT of the non-minimal couplings with coefficients of zero mass dimension. Depending on such non-minimal couplings, gravity can enhance or reduce the region of parameter space where the phase transition completes. Observable consequences of the role of gravity on the FOPT that can be probed by current and future GW detectors are then worked out and we explore the possibility that the background of GWs detected by pulsar timing arrays is produced by FOPTs in the RSB scenario. We also estimate the number of e-folds that elapse when the field playing the role of the order parameter is trapped in the false vacuum, which provides important information for cosmology.

paper.title: Stars Can Quench Superradiance Around Supermassive Black Holes
paper.abstract: Light scalar fields trigger an instability around rotating black holes which drives the rapid growth of high-density bound states on astrophysically short timescales---a phenomenon known as black hole superradiance. This process is usually tacitly assumed to happen independent of the local environment. Around supermassive black holes, however, orbiting stars and compact objects act as a perturbation that drains energy from the cloud, potentially preventing its formation altogether. In this work, we quantify under what conditions this happens, focusing on bound-free state transitions. We first compute the rate of energy dissipation due to gravitational interactions, finding that the superradiance growth rate almost always dominates the environmental depletion. The two rates are, however, close enough that the conclusion could be overturned once bound-bound transitions are included. Also, the environment dissipates the cloud faster than gravitational-wave emission, implying that stellar environments must be accounted for in a variety of indirect search strategies. We then investigate the impact of the scalar's quadratic couplings to nucleons and electromagnetism, showing that these interactions can greatly enhance energy dissipation, preventing the cloud's formation. This work highlights the importance of accounting for the local environment in studies of superradiance around intermediate and supermassive black holes.

paper.title: Beyond Point Photo-$z$ Estimates: Normalizing Flows for Tomographic $N(z)$ Reconstruction with DESI DR1
paper.abstract: Accurate calibration of tomographic redshift distributions, $N(z)$ is essential for cosmological analysis of weak lensing data. We investigate conditional normalizing flows (NFs) and compare their performance with random forest (RF) and quantile random forest (QRF) models. We consider DESI galaxy and quasar targets from DESI DR1 spectroscopic data and with the photometry from Legacy Surveys DR10. We train on 1.1 million sources and test on 2.0 million sources in a non-overlapping sky region ($0<z_{\rm spec}<4.5$). For point estimation, the NF achieves the lowest scatter and outlier fraction at $0<z_{\rm spec}<1.6$ and outperforms both baselines across all three metrics at $z_{\rm spec}>1.6$. By introducing distribution-level metrics like Wasserstein distance and JS divergence, we find that stacking NF posterior PDFs provides more accurate tomographic $N(z)$ reconstruction than QRF, particularly at high redshifts. For $z_{\rm median}>2.5$, the NF achieves a smaller absolute mean-redshift bias ($0.060\pm0.031$ versus $0.318$) and higher probability overlap ($0.905\pm0.008$ versus $0.787$) than QRF. We apply redshift-dependent post-hoc PDF calibration derived from a held-out validation sample. After calibration, the absolute mean-redshift biases in four bins spanning $0.2<z_{\rm median}<1.0$ range from $0.0016$ to $0.0019$, with central values below referring benchmark $0.002(1+z)$. In the highest-redshift bin, calibration further reduces the bias to $0.016\pm0.011$. Our results demonstrate the potential of NF PDFs for tomographic $N(z)$ reconstruction while highlighting challenges in transferring models across galaxy populations.

paper.title: Galaxy cluster thermodynamics at z=1.7: Resolved tSZ and X-ray analysis of CL J0459.6-4946
paper.abstract: Measurements of the entropy and temperature distribution of the intracluster medium (ICM) of local clusters have proven pivotal for the study of cluster astrophysics. Here, we extend these measurements to $z=1.7$ with a resolved analysis of the ICM in ACT/SPT-CL J0459.6-4946. By combining high-resolution thermal Sunyaev-Zeldovich measurements using new, deep ALMA Band 1 and 3 observations, with archival X-ray data, we conclude that the cluster has (i) an ICM with a flat and relatively high ($\approx 200$ keV cm$^2$) entropy distribution out to $\approx 0.3\,r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$, (ii) a hot core ($T_{\mathrm{e}} \simeq 14$ keV) with a declining temperature profile, (iii) a short effective path length along the line of sight of $l_{\mathrm{eff}} \simeq (0.75 \pm 0.05) \times r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$, and (iv) a clumpiness factor $C = \langle n_{\mathrm{e}}^2 \rangle / \langle n_{\mathrm{e}} \rangle^2 \simeq 1.17 \pm 0.05$ within $r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$. Its dynamic nature and high redshift suggest that the cluster is still thermalising its ICM, consistent with a relatively large hydrostatic mass bias of $b = 1 - M_{500,\mathrm{c,HE}}/M_{500,\mathrm{c,WL}} = 0.27^{+0.32}_{-0.67}$ that we measure with respect to the weak lensing mass. Furthermore, a region with low entropy and high density to the south of the cluster centre is observed in the X-rays yet absent in the Compton-$y$ map, indicating pressure equilibrium; we interpret this as a sloshing cold front -- the first such detection at high redshifts. This case study demonstrates that $\approx 3$h-long ALMA observations, combined with comparatively "short" X-ray exposures ($\approx 122$ ks), can fully characterise the ICM at high redshift, opening a path towards the thermodynamics of young and distant galaxy clusters for larger samples.

paper.title: Wide-field search for submicrosecond optical and gamma transients as manifestation of primordial black holes evaporation with the TAIGA-HiSCORE Cherenkov array
paper.abstract: We demonstrated in our papers [Panov, 2021; Panov,2025), that the TAIGA-HiSCORE Cherenkov array physics, originally designed for research in cosmic rays and ultra-high-energy gamma-ray astronomy, can also be used for wide-field searches for very rare submicrosecond optical transients of astrophysical origin. The papers \cite{PANOV-2021,PANOV-2025} presented the results of the first four seasons of optical transient searches (2018--2022) and the resulting upper limits on the flux of corresponding events. The present paper presents data processing from two new seasons of optical transient searches (2022--2024). This paper further develops a method for searching for narrow spatiotemporal groups of ultra-high-energy gamma-rays (above 100\,TeV). Since the evaporation of relic black holes can be accompanied by both by the emission of a short light pulse and by a flash of ultra-high-energy gamma-rays, a multimessenger technique for searching for black hole evaporation was in fact implemented in this work, where two different methods are implemented within a single instrument. The search for narrow spatiotemporal groups of gamma-rays was carried out in time windows of 1000\,$μ$s, 100\,$μ$s, and 6\,$μ$s. Since narrow groups of gamma were not detected, the upper limit on their frequency were obtained as $10^{-3}\,\mathrm{ster}^{-1}\mathrm{h}^{-1}$. The upper limit on the number of submicrosecond optical transients have also been updated: $10^{-4}\mathrm{erg/s/cm}^2$ as $5\cdot10^{-4}\,\mathrm{ster}^{-1}\mathrm{h}^{-1}$.

paper.title: The Devil Went Down to de Sitter: Divergent Effective Field Theory Expansions in Cosmology
paper.abstract: Effective field theories (EFTs) in de Sitter space, and in accelerating cosmologies more generally, must capture phenomena absent in flat space, most notably long-range correlations generated by spontaneous particle production. When heavy physics is integrated out in such time-dependent backgrounds, these effects leave an imprint on the EFT expansion: even at tree level, this is generically an asymptotic rather than convergent series. This is not a failure of EFT. The large-order behavior of the expansion coefficients encodes physical information inaccessible at any finite order, so cosmological EFTs contain hidden data. Using resurgence analysis, we show how this information can be systematically extracted to recover exact and non-perturbative predictions from the perturbative expansion. In the example we study, the resurgent completion is naturally organized in terms of the de Sitter $S$-matrix. This leads us to conjecture a prescription for extracting $S$-matrix data from cosmological EFTs in general. The framework extends to any setting where particle production, or a similar non-perturbative phenomenon, renders the EFT expansion asymptotic. A longer companion paper will provide a more detailed and pedagogical treatment.

paper.title: Hidden Neutrino Active Galaxy Candidates: Prospects for Catalog and Stacking Searches with IceCube, IceCube-Gen2, and KM3NeT
paper.abstract: In high-energy neutrino astrophysics, the identification of high-energy neutrino sources is a central goal, and jet-quiet active galactic nuclei (AGNs) have emerged as promising candidates. For this purpose, we present a theory-guided, intrinsic X-ray selected sample of hidden neutrino AGN candidates consisting of $28$ X-ray bright AGNs (X-HiNAC), combining the {\em Swift}/BAT and BASS surveys with dedicated {\em NuSTAR} observations and spectral analyses. We compile their intrinsic X-ray fluxes, spectral properties, luminosity distances, and supermassive black hole masses, to provide a coherent sample for neutrino source searches. The sample is physically motivated but remains model independent given that the neutrino flux is proportional to the intrinsic X-ray flux. Using the magnetically powered corona model, we also demonstrate the prospects for individual-source and stacking searches with IceCube-Gen2 and KM3NeT. We identify promising individual targets and find that stacking the remaining sources, excluding NGC 1068, could yield a $5σ$ detection within $\sim 5-15$ years under favorable model assumptions at the current and upcoming neutrino observatories. We highlight systematic uncertainties in the adopted source parameters, particularly the black hole masses, for which different measurement techniques can yield estimates differing by up to an order of magnitude. Such uncertainties can significantly affect the predicted neutrino emission, motivating more precise black hole mass measurements and improved broadband X-ray observations. Our findings motivate improved multiwavelength characterization of nearby AGNs and provide a guide for investigating their role as high-energy neutrino sources.

paper.title: Tests of an EP-Preserving Wake Force
paper.abstract: A universal quadratic coupling of ultralight scalar dark matter to ordinary matter preserves the weak equivalence principle for unscreened point particles. A finite test body is nevertheless not a passive probe: it distorts the scalar field that accelerates it. We show that this field distortion produces a differential acceleration between concentric test masses, even when their microscopic coupling is universal. We calculate this signal including how each test mass distorts the field acting on the other, deriving the weak-screening limit and extending the calculation to stronger screening using concentric spherical layers. Applying the model to MICROSCOPE, we find differential signals in both its equivalence-principle sensor SUEP, whose test masses have different compositions, and its reference sensor SUREF, whose test masses have the same composition. We combine both sensors with the dark matter wake near Earth to recast the published MICROSCOPE measurements. Within this model, existing measurements probe scalar masses up to approximately $8 \times 10^{-9}\,$eV and couplings below the supernova bound. An analysis using the additional frequency components of the scalar signal could extend the mass reach and probe couplings below the BBN bound.

paper.title: Lightest and heaviest nuclei as keys to the origin of ultrahigh energy cosmic rays
paper.abstract: The origin of ultrahigh energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) has been a long-standing mystery. A unique feature of UHECRs originating in binary neutron star mergers (BNSMs) is two distinct populations of light elements -- those directly accelerated in the jets, and photo-disintegration products of massive nuclei accelerated in the bulk outflow. We show that Pierre Auger Observatory spectrum and composition data confirm the existence of the predicted two populations at $\geq \!7.2σ$ significance, having rigidity ($R\equiv E/Ze$) cutoffs agreeing with prior estimates. The data also favor 5-10% of UHECRs originating as r-process nuclei, a signature of a BNSM origin. Our results provide strong evidence that UHECRs are produced by merging neutron stars, and show how UHECRs and UHE-neutrinos elucidate otherwise inaccessible aspects of neutron star mergers.

paper.title: Intranight optical monitoring of eight quasars with superluminal jets and low optical polarization: Probing the mechanism of rapid flux variability
paper.abstract: Intranight optical variability (INOV) of blazars whose emission arises predominantly from a relativistic jet, has been widely linked to a combination of two key observational diagnostics: the fractional optical polarization ($P_{opt}$) and the Doppler boost arising from relativistic beaming of the jet's emission. To discern which of these two factors plays the dominant role, we investigate INOV of a well-defined representative sample of 8 flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs, which are `low-synchrotron-peaked' blazars) whose jets exhibit a low degree of polarization ($P_{opt}$ < 3$\%$) but a large superluminal motion with c$β_{app}$ = 5c $-$ 31c (median = 10c). We report sensitive optical monitoring of these 8 `low-polarization superluminal quasars' (LPSQs) using a 1.3-metre telescope, in 20 sessions of minimum 3-hour duration. These data were supplemented with similarly high-quality monitoring data/results available in the literature for this sample, thus adding another 19 sessions. Duty cycle (DC) of strong INOV (amplitude $ψ> 5\%$) is found to be zero, applying the normally used $F_η$ test, and $\sim 7\%$ using the more powerful `enhanced $F$-test'. The small DC, despite the strong Doppler boost expected from the observed high superluminality, shows that strong INOV is much rarer among LPSQs, compared to high-polarization quasars, for which DC $(ψ> 5\%$) is found to be around 30%, even using the $F_η$ test. This provides the first compelling evidence that optical polarization is the primary diagnostic of INOV, while relativistic beaming plays a supportive role. Possible implications for the proposed mechanisms for INOV are pointed out.

paper.title: Dust-induced reversal of the optical wavelength dependence of spiral-arm pitch angles
paper.abstract: The classical density-wave scenario predicts a blue-to-red age--colour gradient across the spiral arms of disc galaxies as a consequence of shock-induced star formation. However, observations of spiral-arm pitch angles at different wavelengths sometimes suggest the opposite trend, namely a red-to-blue ``colour jump''. The origin of this apparent contradiction remains unclear. In this work, we investigate the effects of dust attenuation on post-shock stellar emission, together with the streamline motions of gas and stellar populations. We find that dust attenuation in regions with relatively high optical depths, $\hatτ_{V} \gtrsim 0.2$, can produce an apparent red-to-blue spatial sequence, with respect to the shock location, by reversing the relative positions of the flux maxima of stellar populations observed in different bands. Moreover, streamline motions confine post-shock stellar populations near the spiral arms for longer than in a circular-orbit model, thereby modifying the spatial distribution of the emitted light. We conclude that the apparent red-to-blue colour jump does not necessarily contradict the classical density-wave scenario. Instead, it can arise from the same post-shock stellar populations that intrinsically produce a blue-to-red age--colour gradient if their emission is modified by dust attenuation.

paper.title: A local action for Kodaira--Spencer gravity
paper.abstract: A local action is given for Kodaira--Spencer gravity by solving a constraint on the complex structure deformation of a Calabi--Yau threefold in terms of a $(1,1)$ form as the new gravity field. The gauge algebra becomes a genuine $L_{\infty}$ algebra based on a Courant algebroid, while the gravity field and its linearized gauge transformations coincide with those of double field theory. On a real three-dimensional slice, the free action reduces to the Fierz--Pauli action for massless spin-2 plus the Kalb--Ramond action for a B-field. Non-linearly, the theory carries parity-odd interactions with three derivatives, and it is gauge invariant without a level-matching constraint, in this sense defining an unconstrained double field theory. The full theory is encoded in a cyclic $L_{\infty}$ algebra, for which a double copy interpretation is given.

paper.title: A VLT/CRIRES+ study of helium 1.083$μ$m absorption features towards the inner Orion Nebula
paper.abstract: JWST NIRCam F115W observations towards the inner Orion Nebula revealed a diverse array of previously unknown dark features. The most likely cause was absorption or suppressed emission of the helium 1.083$μ$m triplet which lies in that filter. We have obtained VLT/CRIRES+ high-resolution spectrographic observations over a selection of different dark targets, confirming that the features are indeed explained by a reduction in the flux of the helium 1.083$μ$m triplet, a reduction that is fairly uniform across the line. The Orion Nebula is a blister HII region, with a dense, bright ionised layer on the far side from the observer near the Orion A molecular cloud and lower density gas elsewhere. Using a simple radiative transfer model, we show that dark features arise when emission from the dense layer is absorbed by intermediate density helium (e.g. in clumps, globules, or winds from objects like proplyds) on the near side of the dense layer.
